page.h1: Best LiFePO4 battery charger for 12 V batteries
page.desc: The best LiFePO4 battery charger for a 12 V 100 Ah battery is the Redodo 14.6V 20A: about 5 hours to full, wakes a BMS-shut battery, $20 less than LiTime. Plus 10 A and 40 A picks.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best LiFePO4 battery charger for a 12 V battery is the Redodo 14.6V 20A LiFePO4 Battery Charger ({buy:redodo-14-6v-20a-lifepo4-charger}): it holds 14.6 V at 20 A, so it charges a 100 Ah battery in about 5 hours, and its pre-charge stage wakes a battery whose BMS has shut off. That shut-off is the problem owners ask about most: a lithium battery left too long reads near 0 V at the terminals, and an ordinary charger sees nothing to charge. The Redodo feeds a small pre-charge current until the BMS reconnects, then runs the normal constant-current and constant-voltage stages and stops. It is the same design, output and 2-year warranty as the LiTime 12V 20A, for $20 less on 2026-11-06.

Match the current to the battery. 20 A suits 100 Ah to 200 Ah. For 20 Ah to 50 Ah batteries use the 10 A Redodo ({buy:redodo-14-6v-10a-lifepo4-charger}), because small batteries often limit charge current to 0.5C. For 200 Ah and larger banks, a 40 A charger halves the wait; LiTime's 12V 40A was the cheaper of the two 40 A units today.

page.after:
What owners complain about

Five themes come up again and again in reviews and forum threads for 14.6 V chargers.

  • The charger won't start on a dead battery. The most common thread. A LiFePO4 battery's BMS disconnects the terminals at its low-voltage limit, usually around 10 V, and the battery then reads near 0 V. A lead-acid charger or a lithium charger without an activation stage refuses to charge it. Epoch Batteries warns against forcing voltage in from an uncontrolled source; a charger with a pre-charge or activation function is the safe fix, and every charger in the table except the Victron has one.
  • Fan noise. Five separate owners of Redodo, LiTime and ECO-WORTHY 20 A units call the fan loud or noticeable. It runs the whole time the charger is at full current. Charge in a garage or compartment, not next to a bed.
  • Current below the rating. Three owners measured 10 A to 16 A rather than 20 A. Some of that is the normal taper in the constant-voltage stage, and some is cable loss: one owner measured 14.6 V at the charger and 13.8 V at the battery through thin leads. Keep the output lead short and tight.
  • The charger says full but the monitor shows 95%. Usually the battery monitor has drifted, not the charger. A LiFePO4 battery rests at 13.4 V to 13.6 V after a full 14.6 V charge, and a shunt monitor needs that full cycle to re-sync.
  • No charge below freezing. The battery's BMS blocks charging at or below 32°F and the charger shows a fault or zero current. That is the battery protecting itself; warm it indoors or buy a self-heating battery.

Owners also ask whether the charger can stay connected. A dedicated LiFePO4 charger stops at the end of the constant-voltage stage, so leaving it on is fine for days; for storage of a month or more, unplug it and leave the battery at roughly 50% to 70%.

Which charger by battery size

  • 100 Ah to 200 Ah (most RV, trolling and solar batteries): the Redodo 14.6V 20A ({buy:redodo-14-6v-20a-lifepo4-charger}). 20 A is 0.2C on a 100 Ah battery, inside every maker's limit, and a full charge takes about 5 hours.
  • 20 Ah to 50 Ah (fish finders, kayaks, scooters): the Redodo 14.6V 10A ({buy:redodo-14-6v-10a-lifepo4-charger}). A 20 A charger would push 1C into a 20 Ah battery, which many small BMS boards refuse.
  • 200 Ah and up: LiTime's 12V 40A charger at $167.19 on 2026-11-06, or Redodo's 40 A with handle ({buy:redodo-14-6v-40a-lifepo4-charger}) if you prefer its pre-charge mode and wall mount. Check that your battery allows 40 A of charge current first.
  • One charger for a lead-acid car battery and a lithium house battery: the NOCO Genius10. Its 12 V lithium mode is 14.6 V at 10 A, so a 100 Ah battery takes 10 hours or more. It sold for $99.95 at BatteryStuff on 2026-11-06.
  • On a boat: the Victron Blue Smart IP65 12/15 is sealed, 15 A and shows charge progress on your phone; a US dealer listed it at $175.95 on 2026-11-06. One dealer notes the built-in lithium preset may not match a non-Victron battery, so set a custom 14.4 V to 14.6 V profile in the app. Redodo's IP65 10 A waterproof model ($92.99 on 2026-11-06) is the cheaper sealed option.

Not recommended

  • Any lead-acid charger without a lithium mode. Most never reach 14.6 V, so the battery stops at 90% or so, and desulfation pulses can trip the BMS.
  • The NOCO Genius10 as the only charger for a 100 Ah battery. 10 A is too slow for daily use, and its Force mode disables protections while it runs.
  • Vatrer's 14.6V 20A. It was $74.99 but out of stock on 2026-11-06; its 70 A model at $269.99 only makes sense for 300 Ah and larger banks.
